name: VelisChat
author: velislab

sections.description:
VelisChat adds an AI assistant to your site. You tell it about your business, pick the pages, posts and other content it should learn from, and it answers your visitors’ questions in their own language. When a visitor wants to get in touch, the chatbot shows a contact form and the request reaches you by email, with the conversation attached.

You use your own account with the AI service you prefer: Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude or OpenAI ChatGPT. VelisChat talks to it through the AI features of WordPress: you connect the service once, in Settings → Connectors, and VelisChat never sees or stores your API key. VelisChat has no monthly limits and needs no license.

What it does

  • Answers visitors with what you wrote about your business and with the pages, posts and custom post types you selected (products, services, rooms, courses… created by your theme or other plugins)
  • Shows a contact form when a visitor asks to be contacted, or after they gave the information you need
  • Sends you the contact request by email, with the conversation attached
  • Two layouts: a text bar at the bottom of the page, or a compact icon in a corner
  • Three color styles (Default, Light, Dark), your own main color, and six fonts included in the plugin
  • Works on multilingual sites (WPML and Polylang): the assistant answers in the visitor’s language and links to the page in that language
  • A limit on the requests from one address and on the messages of a single conversation, since every answer is paid by you to the AI service: you set both in the settings, or turn them off
  • A test mode: only administrators see the chatbot until you are ready
  • A setup wizard

VelisChat Pro

VelisChat Pro is a separate, paid add-on sold on velislab.it. It adds more ready-made styles and full control of the colors, your own logo, chat history and statistics, a summary of the conversation in the contact emails, automatic summaries of long content, texts for each language, The Events Calendar events and, in its Ecommerce version, your WooCommerce catalog with product cards and cart. VelisChat works without it.

External services

VelisChat sends its requests to the AI service you choose in its settings through the AI Client of WordPress (wp_ai_client_prompt()), with the connector and the API key you set up in Settings → Connectors. The plugin itself makes no request to the AI services and never handles the API key. Nothing is sent before the service is connected, and visitors’ messages are sent only after they have read which service receives them.

For every message of a visitor, the plugin sends the message, the conversation so far, your instructions and the content you selected. To pick the plugin’s model, WordPress may ask the service for its list of models. Only if an administrator clicks “Move the saved key to Connectors” (after updating from a version before 1.0), the API key saved by the old version is sent to the service to check that it works, then moved to Settings → Connectors.

Google Gemini API

Used when you choose Gemini.
Service provided by Google: terms of service, privacy policy.

Anthropic API (Claude)

Used when you choose Claude.
Service provided by Anthropic: terms of service, privacy policy.

OpenAI API (ChatGPT)

Used when you choose ChatGPT.
Service provided by OpenAI: terms of use, privacy policy.

VelisLab support

Only when an administrator fills in and sends the form of the “Support” page, the plugin emails the request to VelisLab with the site’s address, the plugin version, the administrator’s name and email address, the message and the attached screenshots.

Third-party libraries

  • Fira Sans, Open Sans, Lato, Montserrat, Nunito and Lora fonts, SIL Open Font License, served from the plugin’s own files.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (it needs WordPress 7.0 or later).
  2. In Settings → Connectors, install the connector of the AI service you want to use (OpenAI, Google or Anthropic) and enter its API key.
  3. Follow the setup wizard: choose the same AI service, set the email address for the contact requests, tell the assistant about your business.
  4. Turn off the test mode when you are ready: the chatbot appears to your visitors.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account with an AI service?

Yes. You need an API key of Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude or OpenAI, entered in Settings → Connectors. The plugin’s settings link to the page where each service gives you one.

I used a version before 1.0: what happens to my API key?

Up to version 0.9 VelisChat kept the API key in its own settings. From 1.0 the key lives in Settings → Connectors, where WordPress keeps it for every plugin that uses AI. After the update, the plugin’s settings show a button that moves the saved key there once you have installed the service’s connector; the old copy is then deleted.

How much does it cost?

There are two separate costs:

  1. The plugin: VelisChat is free. The optional Pro add-on is a subscription paid to VelisLab and covers the plugin’s features, not the AI.
  2. The AI: you pay it directly to the AI service you chose (OpenAI, Google or Anthropic), with prepaid credit on your account with that service. You top it up by hand or automatically, and every answer of the chatbot uses a little of it. VelisLab never receives this money.

The settings page shows an estimate of the cost of 1,000 conversations for each service.

What happens if my AI credit runs out?

The AI service stops answering, so the chatbot stops too: visitors who write to it are offered the contact form, so no request is lost. VelisChat sends you an email and shows a notice in the WordPress admin with a link to top up. Once the credit is back, the chatbot starts again by itself within a few minutes.

To avoid it, turn on automatic top-up in your account with the AI service and set a monthly limit.

Which content does the assistant know?

What you write in “Instructions and content” and the pages, posts and custom post types you select there. It never reads content you did not select, password-protected content or drafts.

Can the assistant tell visitors the price and availability of my WooCommerce products?

No. VelisChat reads the text of the products you select (name and description), but not their prices, stock or variations, which change without the product being edited. The assistant is told not to quote prices or availability and to send visitors to the product page for them. The Ecommerce version of the VelisChat Pro add-on reads the catalog from WooCommerce, with prices and availability.

Does the assistant know the dates of my The Events Calendar events?

Only if they are written in the event’s text. VelisChat reads the text of the events you select, but not the dates, times, venue, organizer and cost that The Events Calendar keeps apart: the assistant is told to state them only when the text says them, and to send visitors to the event page. The VelisChat Pro add-on reads them from The Events Calendar.

Is there a limit on the messages?

Only the ones you set, to keep your AI costs under control. In “Settings” you choose how many messages a visitor can send in one conversation before being offered the contact form (50 on a new site, 0 for no limit) and how many requests one address can send in an hour (30 on a new site, or turned off). Site administrators have no limits.

Is a “Powered by” link shown on my site?

Only if you turn it on in “Design and texts”. It is off by default.

What happens to the visitors’ messages?

They are sent to the AI service you chose to get an answer, and kept in the visitor’s PHP session to continue the conversation. Before the first message, visitors are told which service receives their messages. The plugin itself stores no conversation.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • If a connector in Settings → Connectors stops with an error while starting (usually because some WordPress files are missing after an update cut short), the site no longer shows “There has been a critical error”: that AI service just stays not connected, and a notice explains how to fix it by reinstalling WordPress in Dashboard → Updates.

1.0

  • VelisChat uses the AI features of WordPress 7.0: the AI services are connected in Settings → Connectors, with their official connectors, and the plugin no longer calls them directly nor keeps the API key. WordPress 7.0 or later is required.
  • The settings and the setup wizard show whether the chosen service is connected and what is missing.
  • After the update, the API key saved by the previous version can be moved to Settings → Connectors with one click; it is then deleted from the plugin’s settings.

0.9.10

  • The assistant reads the selected content as text with every AI service: the plugin no longer builds a PDF file with it, and no longer uploads a file to Gemini. The FPDF library is no longer included.
  • “Instructions and content” shows the text the assistant reads, with the “Show text” button.
  • The old content PDF and its folder in wp-content/uploads are deleted after the update.

0.9.9

  • The image at the start of the chat field stays visible on themes that place their text fields above the other elements (before, it could be hidden behind the field).
  • The chatbot no longer reads the sample texts that some themes leave in their elements (for example “here’s some awesome text that would only be shown on hover” in the Salient fancy box). The selected contents are read again once after the update.

0.9.8

  • For developers: new filters to change the requests for generated texts and to add other kinds of content to the chatbot’s document. Nothing changes in how the plugin works.

0.9.7

  • Site names with an apostrophe or other special characters are shown correctly in the chat, in the privacy notice and in the emails (before, “‘” could appear instead of the apostrophe).

0.9.6

  • Sections switched off or hidden on every device in WPBakery and Elementor are no longer read by the chatbot: it only tells visitors what they can see on the page. The selected contents are read again once after the update.

0.9.5

  • Checked again with Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT: nothing changes in how the plugin works.

0.9.4

  • When the contact form opens, the assistant introduces it with a sentence of its own, in the language the visitor is writing in.

0.9.3

  • The maximum number of messages of a conversation is set in “Settings”, where it can also be turned off.
  • The bundled FPDF library deletes its temporary files and escapes its error messages the WordPress way.

0.9.2

  • The Events Calendar events: a note under their instructions explains that VelisChat reads their text but not their dates, venue, organizer and cost, and the assistant is told to state those only when the event’s text says them.

0.9.1

  • WooCommerce products: a note under their instructions explains that VelisChat reads their text but not their prices, stock or variations, and the assistant is told not to quote prices or availability from them.

0.9

  • Posts and custom post types (products, services, rooms, courses…) can be selected as content, with their own instructions.
  • Your own main color, in “Design and texts”.
  • The limit on the messages of a conversation can be changed in wp-config.php or with a filter.
  • The conversation kept in the session is checked and cleaned every time it is read or written.
  • The plugin’s main file is now velischat.php, and the bundled FPDF library has its own class name so it can’t clash with other plugins.
  • The translations come from translate.wordpress.org.

0.8.7

  • The email sent when the AI credit runs out is now formatted like the contact email, with a button to top up the credit.

0.8.6

  • “How paying works” in the settings and in the setup wizard: the plugin and the AI are paid separately, the AI with prepaid credit on your account with the AI service, and the chatbot stops when that credit reaches zero.
  • When the AI credit runs out, VelisChat notices it: you get an email and a notice in the admin with a link to top up, and visitors are offered the contact form instead of an error. The chatbot starts again by itself once the credit is back.

0.8.5

  • Right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian…): on sites in these languages the chatbot is mirrored, with the icon on the bottom left in the compact layout.
  • Messages follow the direction of their own text: a visitor writing in Arabic on a site in another language, or in English on an Arabic site, reads every message aligned on the right side.

0.8.4

  • Contact email: the field names and the month in the date of the attached conversation are now in the site’s main language, also when the visitor writes in another one.

0.8.3

  • Code annotations for the WordPress.org review (Plugin Check): nothing changes in how the plugin works.

0.8.2

  • Fixed: the assistant sometimes answered in the language of the site’s content instead of the visitor’s (with Gemini and Claude about one time in four, sometimes with ChatGPT).
  • The translations of translate.wordpress.org are used first; the ones included in the plugin cover the languages that don’t have them yet.
  • The folder with the content PDF is now wp-content/uploads/velischat: the old velis-chatbot folder is moved automatically.

0.8.1

  • Fixed: the chat answered every question with an error, because its requests had been renamed in 0.8 and the server didn’t recognize them. The form for leaving your details and the “Clear chat” button were affected too.
  • An administrator trying the chat sees the technical cause of an error (visitors still get a generic message).

0.8

  • VelisChat is free and needs no license. The paid features are now a separate add-on, VelisChat Pro.
  • English is the plugin’s base language; Italian, French and Spanish translations are included.
  • The “VelisChat is the AI chatbot for WordPress” line is off unless the site owner turns it on.
  • The requests to the AI services use the WordPress HTTP API.
  • The banner that presents VelisChat Pro can be hidden for 30 days with its close button.
  • The instructions given to the AI are in English on every site: the assistant answers in the visitor’s language (or in the one the site’s instructions ask for) and addresses visitors informally.
